item.title: Version 1.9.2
item.description:
Mila 1.9.2

The stable release of everything in the 1.9.2 betas, plus the fixes that came out of testing them.

New

  • Pause and resume a recording. Long meetings have stretches you don't want captured at all — a side conversation, a break, someone reading a password out loud. Pause leaves that span genuinely absent from the audio rather than recorded as silence, and the timer stops while you're paused.
  • Microsoft Teams meetings are detected, alongside Zoom. Mila offers to start recording when a Teams call begins and offers to stop when it ends, using the same reliable audio signal it uses for Zoom rather than guessing from window titles.
  • Send your transcripts to Obsidian. Point Mila at a vault in Settings → Storage and every finished recording is written there as a Markdown note — title, date, duration, summary, action items, transcript. Off by default; nothing happens until you choose a vault.
  • Bring your own AI provider — no local CLI required. Summaries, action items and recording names can now talk to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Ollama Cloud, a local Ollama, or your own server. The existing Claude and Cursor CLI options are untouched, and Gemini CLI joins them.
  • Empty Trash. Clear everything in Recently Deleted in one action instead of deleting rows one at a time. It tells you how many recordings it will delete and asks first.
  • AI settings are reorganised into two tabs. *AI Provider* is where you configure your AI once; *AI Features* is where you turn each feature on and edit its prompt, one expandable section per feature. Your existing provider, API key and prompts carry over untouched.

Transcription

  • English recordings on a Hebrew server no longer come back with Hebrew words in them. If your transcription server runs a Hebrew model like ivrit.ai, Settings → Models now has an English model field so English recordings go to a multilingual model while Hebrew keeps using the accurate Hebrew one. Leave it blank if your server already handles every language.
  • The recording language is Hebrew or English — Auto-detect is gone. Mila picks which speech model to use *from* that choice, so "let it detect" meant guessing which specialist to ask before knowing what language it needed to handle. Picking the language in the toolbar is one click and gives a noticeably better transcript.
  • Transcription progress no longer sticks or jumps backwards. The progress bar now only ever moves forward, and the app stays responsive during long transcriptions.

Recording reliability

  • Unplugging your headphones mid-meeting no longer silently stops the recording. If the microphone Mila was recording from went away — a wired headset unplugged, a Bluetooth headset switching profile, another app taking the device — capture used to die on the spot while the timer kept counting: one user's 26-minute call was saved as 24 seconds of audio. Mila now notices within seconds and picks the recording back up on whichever microphone is available.
  • Dictation and recording no longer capture silence on some Macs. A repair meant to recover from that device change could retrigger itself on certain audio setups, restarting capture several times a second so nothing was ever recorded — and the failure surfaced as a confusing "failed to decode" error from the transcription server. Fixed, with the microphone indicator no longer flickering.
  • Recordings recovered after a crash now transcribe. A crash or force-quit left the audio file's header unfinished, so every reader — including Mila's own transcription — saw an empty file even though the audio was all there on disk. Those recordings are repaired on the next launch.
  • Renaming, filing or deleting a recording while it transcribes now sticks. Those edits used to be silently reverted when the transcription finished.
  • App audio comes back on its own if macOS drops the other side of a meeting part way through, and a recording that captured far less audio than the time you spent recording now says so plainly instead of leaving you to discover it in the transcript.
  • A recording's length comes from the audio itself, so a capture that ended early no longer claims the full duration.

Fixes

  • The live transcript stays with the newest words instead of drifting out of view and needing to be scrolled by hand.
  • Stopping a recording really stops the AI. The Live AI session could fire one more request after Stop and leave a temporary folder behind.
  • All Settings tabs are reachable. With ten tabs the window was too narrow, so the last ones collapsed into a >> menu and looked disabled. The Updates tab has also moved into General — its automatic-update and beta options are there now.
  • Beta builds are no longer offered to people who didn't ask for them. A pre-release published without its channel marker was offered to everyone; Mila now refuses pre-release updates unless you've enabled beta versions in Settings → General.

item.title: Version 1.9.2-beta.3
item.description:
Mila 1.9.2-beta.3

  • If you installed beta 2, dictation and recording could capture nothing at all — that's fixed. On some Macs the microphone indicator flickered rapidly, the recording came out empty, and transcription then failed with "Failed to decode audio", which looked like the transcription server was down when it wasn't. The recovery added in beta 2 was reacting to a change it had caused itself, restarting the microphone about seven times a second so no audio was ever captured. Beta 2 has been withdrawn; this build replaces it. Mila now also refuses to send an empty recording for transcription, and tells you no audio was captured instead of showing a server error you can't act on.
  • Unplugging your headphones mid-meeting no longer silently stops the recording. If the microphone Mila was recording from went away — USB EarPods or a wired headset unplugged, a Bluetooth headset switching profile, another app taking the device — macOS quietly swapped in a different mic and Mila's capture died on the spot. The timer kept counting and the recording looked normal in the list, but nothing after that moment was actually recorded: one user's 26-minute Zoom call was saved as 24 seconds of audio. Mila now notices within a few seconds and picks the recording back up on whichever microphone is available, so you lose a moment instead of the meeting.
  • App audio (the other side of a meeting) comes back on its own if macOS drops it. When the system audio capture died part way through a recording, Mila silently continued with just your own microphone. It now restarts that capture and writes down what happened, so a half-captured meeting is something you can see rather than something you discover in the transcript.
  • Recordings show how long they actually are. A recording's length came from the timer that ran while you recorded, so a capture that ended early still claimed the full length — a 24-second file listed as 26:24. The length now comes from the audio itself.
  • AI setup is now two tabs instead of one crowded one. Settings → AI Provider is where you pick Claude, Cursor or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint once, and Settings → AI Features is where you turn on what Mila does with it — automatic summaries, suggested recording names, your own Send-to-LLM prompt, and Live AI — each an expandable row with its own switch and prompt. Everything you had configured carries over untouched. Output language moved to the AI Features tab, since it governs summaries too, not just Live AI.
  • Live AI now tells you when it can't run. The switch is greyed out with the reason when your setup doesn't support it — previously you could turn it on, record, and get nothing back.
  • Every Settings tab is visible again. The window was too narrow for its own tab bar, so the last tab collapsed into a » menu and looked disabled. The window is wider, and the Updates settings moved into a new General tab rather than having a tab of their own.
  • Beta builds can no longer reach you if you didn't ask for them. A pre-release published without its channel marker was offered to everyone on 30 July. Mila now refuses a pre-release version outright unless you've ticked "Receive beta versions of Mila".
  • Self-hosted Hebrew servers get the English model filled in for you. If your transcription endpoint runs an ivrit.ai model, Mila pre-fills the separate English model field instead of leaving it blank, so English recordings stop coming back with Hebrew words spliced in. Clear the field by hand and Mila leaves it cleared.

item.title: Version 1.9.2-beta.1
item.description:
Mila 1.9.2-beta.1

  • English recordings on a remote server no longer come back with Hebrew words in them. If your transcription server runs a Hebrew model (like ivrit.ai), it stays Hebrew-only no matter what language you pick — Mila asked it for English and it answered with Hebrew words spliced into the text. Settings → Models now has an English model field: set it to your server's multilingual model and English recordings go there, while Hebrew keeps using the accurate Hebrew one. Leave it blank if your server already handles every language (OpenAI's whisper-1, for example) and nothing changes.
  • The recording language is now Hebrew or English — Auto-detect is gone. Mila picks which speech model to use *from* that choice, so "let it detect" meant guessing which specialist to ask before knowing what language it needed to handle — and on a Hebrew-specialised model it rendered English speech as Hebrew, the exact thing Auto-detect was supposed to prevent. Picking the language in the toolbar is one click and gives a noticeably better transcript. If you had Auto-detect selected, Mila switches you to Hebrew; existing Auto-detect recordings keep working and can still be re-transcribed.
  • Bring your own AI provider — no local CLI required. Live AI summaries and action items can now talk to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Ollama Cloud, a local Ollama, or your own server. Previously Mila needed the claude or cursor-agent command-line tool installed on your Mac. Set it up in Settings → Live AI; the existing CLI option is untouched if you're happy with it.
  • Stopping a recording now really stops the AI. The Live AI session kept running briefly after Stop — it could fire one more summary request against a recording Mila had already finished writing, and left its temporary session folder behind. Stop now shuts the session down immediately. Your summary is unaffected: it's regenerated from the complete transcript either way.

item.title: Version 1.9.1
item.description:
Mila 1.9.1

  • Notes for one meeting stay with that meeting. The Live AI pane now has its own Context box for what you want Mila to know about the meeting you're in — the agenda, who's on the call, acronyms it won't recognise. Mila uses them to understand what it hears, never summarises them, never turns them into action items, and clears them when the recording stops. Previously the only place to put that was the system prompt in Settings → Live AI, which applies to every recording — so one meeting's agenda quietly became the next meeting's context, and the summary came back covering both.

item.title: Version 1.9.0
item.description:
Mila 1.9.0

The first stable release of the 1.9.0 line — a big one, with everything since 1.8.14.

New

  • Transcribe on a remote server. Point Mila at any OpenAI-compatible API — OpenAI's Whisper, or your own self-hosted model like ivrit.ai — instead of transcribing on-device. Set it up in Settings → Models. Test connection now uploads a short sample clip and shows you the text that comes back, so you can confirm the server actually transcribes (not just that it's reachable).
  • One-click setup with .milaconfig files. Double-click a .milaconfig file and Mila offers to apply it — the transcription server, model, language, and more — after showing you exactly what will change. Perfect for handing a team a ready-made configuration. Settings not named in the file are left untouched.
  • iPhone Voice Memos sync. Mila can import and auto-transcribe the Voice Memos that iCloud syncs from your iPhone. Pick which folders to watch, set a start date so it doesn't backfill years of old recordings, and it files them under a dedicated Voice Memos folder. It only needs access to that one folder — no Full Disk Access.
  • Name your speakers. Rename speaker labels to real names from a persistent, searchable directory — your names are remembered and reused across recordings.
  • Opt into betas. A new Settings → Updates tab lets you enable pre-release builds and move back to stable whenever you like.

Transcription quality

  • Fewer hallucinations. A neural voice-activity detector skips non-speech, so Whisper stops inventing filler text on silence or background noise.
  • Better with quiet built-in mics. Adaptive gain boosts low-volume input so live transcription keeps working on soft laptop microphones.
  • Auto-discard accidental clips. Very short recordings with no speech — hotkey misfires, empty captures — are dropped automatically. Tune the threshold (or turn it off) in Settings → Storage.

Queue & recordings

  • Stop or remove Queue items. Cancel a stuck or unwanted transcription right from the Queue. Stopped items move to Recently Deleted instead of showing up as "Failed."
  • No more stuck "Queued" items after you quit and relaunch mid-transcription.
  • The Record button no longer waits on the final summary of your previous recording — start the next one immediately.
  • A color per speaker when speaker labels are on, so who-said-what is easier to scan.
  • Export SRT subtitles mid-recording from the live transcript.
  • Collapsible "All Transcriptions" section in the sidebar.

AI & summaries

  • Automatic summaries after each recording (toggle in Settings → LLM), a configurable CLI timeout, and a Test panel to debug your LLM setup.

Fixes & reliability

  • A large bug-fix sweep across the transcription engine, audio capture, diarization, and UI, with new regression tests.
  • System audio is no longer dropped when its clock stalls; the diarization setup no longer gets stuck in a repair loop.
  • Locally-built and DMG installs preserve their signing identity so macOS permission grants (mic, screen recording) survive updates.
  • Fixed the stray border around the dictation pill, restored the sidebar's right-click menu, and many smaller fixes.
  • Added CodeQL security scanning to every build.

item.title: Version 1.8.13
item.description:
• Smoother on long recordings — the Live AI assistant updates on a calmer cadence (every 20s by default, adjustable in Settings), and the recording screen no longer redraws the transcript on every audio frame. Noticeably lower CPU.
  • Speaker labels (diarization) are now off by default — they ran a heavy background process. Turn them back on anytime in Settings ▸ Diarization.
  • Hebrew (right-to-left) fixes — the summary, action items, and transcript now align correctly in both the live and saved views, and saved summaries read as clean lines.
  • New: when a Zoom meeting ends, Mila offers to stop the recording.
  • New: a "What's New" preview before you update.
